newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan Sugar buys 2,500T soyoil at tender-buyers.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan Sugar buys 2,500T soyoil at tender-buyers.

text.p: State-owned Taiwan Sugar Corp. bought a shipment of 2,500 tonnes of South American soyoil at a tender on Wednesday, company officials said.
The shipment would be slated for arrival in Taiwan before June 15, a Taiwan Sugar official said.

Company officials declined to give price details. Traders said the shipment was bought on a cost-and-freight basis, with Taiwan sugar paying for offloading, at about US$600 to US$625 per tonne from soyoil supplier Flavor Full Food Inc.
Taiwan's edible oil producers have been cutting their soybean imports and turning to soyoil imports following the outbreak of hog foot-and-mouth disease in March.

Since news of the epidemic broke on March 20, a mass slaughter of nearly three million hogs has caused a significant drop in the island's demand for soymeal feed, forcing edible oil producers to cut soybean crushing to trim soymeal inventories.
Soyoil production also has fallen as the crush rate has been reduced, forcing producers to turn to crude soyoil imports to make up for the shortfall.
Soybean crushing yields two main products, oil and soymeal. Crushing to produce oil would result in a fast-growing surplus of meal for which there is no demand, crushers said.
